Because labetalol causes orthostatic hypotension it is recommended that injections are given to patients when they are lying down and that patients should re- main lying down for the next 3 hours. Labetalol should be withdrawn from patients who de- velop signs of hepatic impairment. Breast feeding. Labetalol is distributed into breast milk, al- though it has been suggested1 that the proportion of a maternal dose likely to be ingested by the infant is very low. In a study2 in 25 patients, the mean concentration of labetalol in breast milk was less than in maternal plasma in patients given doses between 330 and 800 mg daily, although in 1 patient given 1200 mg daily a higher concentration was found in breast milk. In another study,3 the concentration of drug in milk exceeded maternal plas- ma concentration in 2 of 3 mothers, and in 1 infant the plasma- labetalol concentration was similar to that of the mother. Howev- er, no adverse effects have been seen in breast-feeding infants whose mothers were given labetalol, and the American Acade- my of Pediatrics considers4 that it is therefore usually compatible with breast feeding. 1. Pharmacokinetics Labetalol is readily absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, but is subject to considerable first-pass metabo- lism.
